newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains down on strong stg, supply ideas.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains down on strong stg, supply ideas.

text.p: LIFFE wheat and barley fell on the strength of sterling and fading supply concerns, traders said.

The market had been looking for an easier sterling, and the currency's failure to come down helped push prices lower, one trader said. By late European trade the British currency was back above 2.80 marks, after a correction to below 2.78 on Monday.
Talk of coming rain hit new crop prices, he said. And the old crop was looking fundamentally weak. "It's a bit tired and there's enough around," he said.
And steadier U.S. markets made the world look less exciting. "It seems to have gone off a bit," the trader said.
November was the most active on wheat, with 356 of a total of 793 lots traded. It last changed hands 0.75 stg lower at 98.50 stg.
There were bigger falls for the old crop, with front month May 1.90 stg lower at 96.50 stg.
Barley volume was pumped right up by 118 lots on November of a total 128 lots done. November last traded 1.00 stg lower at 95.00 stg.

But almost all of the barley volume, and much of the wheat was accounted for by a 105 lot November/November wheat/barley spread at 3.25 stg. "We seem very expensive on barley, interventionwise and against the continent," the trader said.
